title: Working at Redwood — Roles, Career Ladders, Benefits, Hiring & Onboarding, and Internal Tools (People Ops Update)
author: Maya Thompson
content:
Overview

This consolidated handbook page (People Ops update) summarizes how we work at Redwood, role definitions and career ladders, benefits & perks, hiring and onboarding processes, and the internal tools employees use daily. Use this as a single reference and follow links to team-level or policy pages for detailed procedures.

1) Working at Redwood — orientation highlights

- Mission: Deliver a developer-first inference platform that balances latency, cost, and reliability. Every role contributes to measurable production outcomes.
- Culture and values: Ship responsibly, own outcomes, measure economics, prioritize developer experience, and cultivate inclusive collaboration.
- Hybrid work model: hybrid-first with core collaboration hours 11:00–16:00 PT. Managers set team-specific onsite expectations; exceptions are approved by People Ops.
- Primary contacts: People Ops (people-ops@redwood.example.com), IT Helpdesk (it-support@redwood.example.com), Payroll (payroll@redwood.example.com).

2) Roles and career ladders (overview)

Redwood publishes ladders for Engineering, Product, Design, Data, Applied ML, SRE, and GTM. Ladders are used for leveling, promotions, hiring scorecards, and performance conversations.

Each ladder contains:
- Level title and summary (scope and accountability)
- Examples of typical deliverables and success metrics
- Competencies: technical craft, cross-functional collaboration, leadership, and execution
- Interview rubric excerpts for key levels

Engineering ladder (excerpt):
| Level | Typical scope | Expectations | Example deliverable |
| E1 / IC1 | Team contributor | Delivers small scoped tasks, learns codebase | Fixes, small features with tests |
| E3 / IC3 | Cross-team contributor | Owns medium features, mentors juniors | Integration that includes monitoring and runbook |
| E6 / Senior Staff | Org-level impact | Shapes architecture and roadmap, leads cross-org initiatives | Kernel selection optimization with measurable latency and cost improvement |

Promotion process (high-level):
1. Manager gathers peer and stakeholder feedback using the standard packet template.
2. Manager submits a promotion packet (impact examples, metrics, reviewers).
3. Calibration review by People Ops and a promotion panel.
4. Outcome communicated with development plan and next steps.

3) Benefits & perks (summary)

High-level highlights — refer to Benefits Portal for full plan documents and vendor links.
- Health: medical, dental, vision plan tiers; contractor stipend for eligible roles.
- Financial: 401(k) with employer match (US), equity grants for full-time employees, transparent salary bands per level.
- Time off: baseline 20 days PTO accrual, 10 company holidays, parental leave (primary parent up to 16 weeks paid), caregiver leave.
- Wellness & family support: monthly wellness stipend, EAP, fertility and family-forming assistance.
- Learning & development: annual L&D allowance, conference budget with manager approval.
- Workplace perks: home office stipend, commuter benefits in applicable regions, catered team events and offsites.

Enrollment and changes:
1. New hire receives benefits enrollment packet during offer acceptance and on Day 1 onboarding.
2. Life-event changes: submit Benefits Change form to People Ops with required documentation.
3. Questions: benefits@redwood.example.com.

4) Hiring and onboarding (overview)

Hiring principles:
- Hire for product and operational thinking: candidates who ship measurable, reliable systems.
- Inclusive interviewing: standard scorecards, interviewer training on bias, and diverse panels where possible.

Typical hiring workflow:
1. Requisition + role scorecard approved by hiring manager and finance.
2. Role posted in Greenhouse with interview plan and rubric.
3. Interview loop: recruiter screen, technical loop (coding or system design), cross-functional final loop.
4. Offer created by People Ops; background check and references completed.

New hire onboarding (90-day program):
- Day 0–1: equipment provisioning, account creation (SSO), People Ops orientation, benefits enrollment.
- Week 1: team onboarding, meet key partners, run through first-week checklist.
- Month 1: agree 30/60/90 goals, complete mandatory trainings (security, data handling, SDLC), assigned buddy.
- Months 2–3: own a scoped project, ramp to independent delivery, regular manager 1:1s.

30/60/90 template (example):
- 30 days: complete trainings, ship a small doc or test fix, meet cross-functional partners.
- 60 days: lead a small feature or experiment, present outcome at team demo.
- 90 days: operate independently on recurring tasks, propose an optimization for a workflow.

Essential onboarding checklist:
- Access: Slack, GitHub, Confluence, CI/CD, cloud console; verify least-privilege access.
- Security: complete security training, acceptable use, and set up MFA.
- Tools: confirm IDE, VPN, build/test pipelines, and local dev env.

5) Internal tools — quick-start guide

This list covers team-level default tools and quick-start actions. For step-by-step tutorials see the team runbooks.

- Slack — Owner: Eng Dev — Purpose: company/tactical communications and on-call coordination. Quick start: join #company-all, #announcements, and your team channel; set working hours.

- GitHub — Owner: Eng Dev — Purpose: source control, PR workflows, branch protection. Quick start: enable SSO, add SSH key, follow CONTRIBUTING.md.

- Confluence — Owner: People Ops + Eng Docs — Purpose: canonical docs and runbooks. Quick start: bookmark company-handbook, use templates for runbooks/PRDs.

- Greenhouse — Owner: Talent & People Ops — Purpose: candidate tracking and feedback. Quick start: complete interviewer training and submit scorecards on time.

- Jira / Linear — Owner: Eng Managers — Purpose: issue tracking (team choice). Quick start: link PRs to tickets and follow team board conventions.

- Internal CI/CD — Owner: Eng Infra — Purpose: automated test and deploy pipelines. Quick start: run local tests and ensure branch CI passes before review.

- Redwood Console (Observability) — Owner: Eng Platform — Purpose: monitoring, tracing, cost/latency dashboards, rollouts. Quick start: sign in, subscribe to team dashboards, set alert preferences.

6) Expectations by role in first 6 months

- Engineering: deliver a low-risk, high-value change; own a reliability or performance metric; complete runtime onboarding checklist.
- Product: produce a 90-day plan and coordinate a cross-functional kickoff; ship a scoped improvement.
- SRE/Infra: validate capacity dashboards, run a game-day exercise, publish or update a runbook.

7) FAQ (short answers)

Q: Who approves L&D requests above the individual allowance?
A: Manager for routine approvals; People Ops for exceptions and larger budget items.

Q: How to request parental leave?
A: Submit parental leave form to People Ops with expected dates at least 30 days prior when feasible.

Q: Where to find on-call expectations?
A: Team runbooks under /eng-platform/runbooks and the on-call rota in Slack.

8) Governance, change log, and feedback

Change log:

Governance: People Ops owns handbook content; engineering teams own technical runbooks. Compensation/benefit changes require People Ops + Legal review. Tooling or runbook changes require Engineering leadership review and a small rollout plan.

Feedback: File a handbook update request at people-ops@redwood.example.com or add a Confluence comment on this page.
